# Implemented capabilities

This page records what the current Moguri alpha actually implements, release by
release. It moved here from the README so the README stays a short landing page.
For the broader product vision, which is not a list of implemented features, see
[product vision](vision.md). Remaining work is tracked in
[remaining milestone gaps](remaining-milestone-gaps.md).

The first executable checkpoint includes an **OpenTUI terminal client** and an
**Electron desktop app** sharing one local service. It supports GitHub Copilot
device sign-in, account-enabled model selection, streamed conversations, native
file operations with script/unlisted-website approvals, persistent drafts and queues, distinct
Queue/Steer/Interrupt delivery, stopping owned process groups, restart recovery,
archival/restoration, and basic per-call accounting.
Optional [metadata-only OTLP export](architecture/otlp-export.md) projects
existing execution/accounting records into traces, canonical gauges and opt-in
correlated diagnostic logs, with keychain-only credential headers.
It is off by default, profile-isolated and explicitly reviewed; no prompts,
tool content, terminal data or private names are exported.
Ordinary active-turn input now uses shared live delivery, while first-topic
[chat names](architecture/chat-titles.md) are generated by one separately
budgeted call; explicit names and held/queued input keep their own contracts.
After a round of requests, a [wrap-up turn](architecture/session-lifecycle.md)
commits, publishes the draft PR and follows CI and reviews. Optional
[pull request automation](architecture/pr-automation.md), off by default with
per-repository overrides, reruns CI jobs that failed for transient reasons after
checking GitHub Status, and resolves base conflicts while keeping both sides' features.
Optional [Claude Agent and Codex Agent](architecture/agent-harnesses.md)
sessions run your own installed Claude Code or Codex with your own sign-in, while
Moguri approves their tool calls and keeps the transcript. Both are off by
default; see [setup](setup.md#claude-agent). Besides GitHub Copilot and custom
OpenAI-compatible endpoints (with custom headers), Moguri connects
[OpenRouter, the Anthropic API, the OpenAI API and a ChatGPT account](architecture/hosted-providers.md).

The TUI uses Enter to send and Shift+Enter for newlines; Cmd/Ctrl+Enter holds
active-turn prompts or opens scheduling when idle. Its compact chat-first
client saves and leaves on `exit`, `/exit` or Ctrl+C while the shared service
keeps working; `/stop` remains the turn-stop command. The
layout has a growing input, formatted replies, expandable tool output, clickable
navigation and a focus-safe sidebar. [Terminal controls](setup.md#terminal-navigation-and-shared-themes)
preserve drafts while reading history. [Shared themes](architecture/themes-and-tui.md)
include ten presets in Dark and Light, without changing saved choices or factory
Dark. Moguri includes its own verified [source setup instructions](setup.md)
in normal model context, including project-free chats. Desktop Settings keeps
on-screen text short; the [Settings reference](settings/README.md) holds
each page's full behavior and safeguards.
The [Local website allowlist](architecture/native-network-policy.md) supports
session, project and profile-wide grants through Guardrails and `/firewall`.

The **importable Moguri SDK** now powers the CLI, TUI and desktop. It exposes
shared editable/restorable system instructions and permissions, opt-in local
vector/graph and coding-style memory, standard skills, reviewed evolution
proposals, curated/approved scripts, declarative plugins, optional tool-less
subagents and one native MCP gateway. Desktop starts dark and uses Moguri's
original face-and-bat-wing mascot.
The mascot now also carries its small red antenna pom-pom.

The [Plan sidebar](architecture/task-progress.md) shows only an explicit
multi-step model checklist, with long-task estimates separately labeled as advice,
never proof of completion. [Session controls](architecture/session-interactions.md)
include ordered drag/drop, context-menu actions, serial held queues and explicit
work/question/approval/completion indicators with verified draft/open/merged PR state.
Unread names use subtle font weight rather than extra session-list dots.
Center drops nest sessions, create named project folders or add a project to an
existing group (groups never nest); folder chats capture
all member repositories for explicit Local reads, edits and commands. Fuzzy
session/settings search and compact settings controls share the
[session reliability contract](architecture/session-reliability.md).
The [Dashboard](setup.md#workspace-experience-and-skill-gateway) follows
active sessions and opens their exact conversations. Its
[Analytics](architecture/session-analytics.md) page draws running and
recent turns on a zoomable lane timeline, kept in memory for an hour only. Project settings select
registered projects; project-group menus fold only their member folders.
**Settings / Repositories** accepts reviewed URL/bullet lists for bulk import, and
[workspace folders](setup.md#adding-a-workspace-folder): trust a folder such as
`~/workspace` and Moguri adds its Git repositories as read-only projects, optionally
kept in sync. Their sessions always work in Moguri-owned worktrees, never the original checkout.
Project settings also reviews [remote URL changes](setup.md#importing-repositories-and-changing-a-remote)
across the actual shared-worktree boundary, without fetching or rewriting old PR sources.
Built-in work-item views remove hidden Markdown comments.
[Repository-script review](architecture/content-review.md) delivers the
full exact source to the agent before execution approval; unsafe findings need
separate actual-user force and never lift hard policy.

Protocol98 adds [Local skill source admission and per-turn rewind](architecture/skills-and-rewind.md).
Complete source/provenance review, expiring grants, least-privilege restrictions
and actual-user revocation share the service, SDK and clients. Reviewed rewind
supports Local, pinned SSH and private Sandbox workspaces while preserving
external edits, current Git intent, later history and spent/unknown budgets.
Sandbox reviewed-script execution remains unqualified; the wider skills-safety
work is not complete.

Protocol99 adds a [session Inbox and explicit skill-load indicators](architecture/session-inbox.md).
Inbox follows Dashboard, opens the owning conversation and supports independent
notification deletion without answering or approving. Successful source loads
show their actual skill name and book icon; discovery is not loading.

[Model recovery and scheduled prompts](architecture/recovery-scheduling-kupo.md)
share the same service and SDK. Transient model failures use current-profile
30/90/120/180-second recovery rounds, without replaying earlier tools or hooks.
The primary button retries the original eligible failure without sending a new
draft. Idle scheduling offers local-time controls, unsent ghost prompts and an
Automations / Scheduled prompts group, with one-at-most queue admission.
[Customize and Artifacts tabs](architecture/skills-tools-artifacts.md) sit next
to Automations: toggle installed skills, install skills from configured
repositories, browse the agent's toolsets, write or ask the agent for script
tools for every chat, and find each project's builds, files, images and links
with their chat. Agents get typed GitHub reads (tags, releases, annotations,
contents, settings, rules) and reviewed `github_write` (comments, threads,
releases, settings; draft PRs only).
An optional recurring check suggests script tools for requests you repeat.
Local and SSH continuation are qualified. A rolled-back native workspace keeps
its explicit inspection/preparation gate instead of automatic root substitution.

Closing or quitting the desktop app saves unsent drafts and open queued-prompt
edits first. Chats a quit, restart or crash interrupted can be
[continued](architecture/interrupted-sessions.md) one by one, all at once,
or automatically after every restart.

[Automations](architecture/automations.md) run a prompt or a declarative
workflow of prompts and repository-trusted scripts once, every N minutes, daily
or on chosen weekdays. Each run starts a new chat in its project with captured
controls; script steps run without a model call under normal approval. Missed
times run once, overlapping times are skipped, and restarts never replay a step.
Desktop, TUI (`/automations`, F9) and CLI (`moguri automations`, YAML/JSON
workflow files) share the same state.

The owner-requested [protocol-41 platform extension](architecture/platform-workflows.md)
adds **Sky/Terra/Glacier knowledge**, reviewed lifecycle hooks and immutable
repository-backed marketplace bundles. Imports/updates/rollbacks stay disabled;
knowledge injection has a separate default-off consent. Nothing self-approves
or starts a model merely because it was installed.

**Local Git built-ins** cover status/history/diff, branch creation/switch/rename,
exact staging, selected staged commits, history-preserving rollback and new-branch
pushes through the same SDK and agent tools. [Usage and boundaries](setup.md#reliable-session-controls-and-built-in-git).
**GitHub workflows** expose exact-root reviewed main/force-with-lease pushes,
rebases, tags, two-way issue/PR/review work, pinned CI watching, releases and
exact-head PR merges. **Linear workflows** add team-scoped issue/project/comment
operations and explicit conflict-checked ticket pull/push. Both retain original
intent/results without replaying ambiguous writes. Dependency caching extends
to explicit private npm registries, npm/pnpm workspaces, Python, Rust/Cargo and
Go; mutable installs remain private and executable builds are not implied.
Desktop exposes the same APIs under Settings; shared `/git`, `/github`, `/linear`,
`/knowledge`, `/hooks`, `/marketplace` and `/cache` commands reach TUI/CLI.

Protocol100 moves [repository-script assessments to Inbox](setup.md#work-item-comments-and-repository-scripts)
with collapsible source and explicit user approval, separate from execution.
Startup shows the original mascot on black with an optional Space-to-flap game.
Inline code stays plain text; fenced blocks keep explicit copy controls.
Missing files say **Not Found**, and provider failures retain their redacted diagnostic.

Protocol101 adds [explicit repo trust, worktree/PR defaults and recoverable output](architecture/repository-workflow-defaults.md).
Existing exact trusted script entrypoints skip model assessment, not approvals;
new/package/generated scripts stay outside the baseline. New single-project
Local Git tasks use managed worktrees and normally finish at a draft PR.
Inbox has search and type/read filters. Qualified partial results can continue;
uncertain effects retain enforced read-only recovery, never false success.

Protocol96 added [original-owner startup reconnect](setup.md#opening-and-last-view-restoration)
and a default-on option to keep agents working when the last window closes.
Explicit Quit still stops the service and known user terminals. Startup
confirmation, private ownership and unsent drafts remain protected; the
original unreproduced 90-second initialization delay is not claimed resolved.

Protocol95 added the [unified My Work inbox](setup.md#unified-my-work):
explicitly configured repositories/accounts, deduplicated PR/review/failed-CI/
unresolved-thread attention, source freshness and retained read-only refresh.
CLI, TUI and desktop share the same SDK, original CI watches and exact scoped
follow-up review. Opening an item never starts polling or grants permission.
The existing active-session and usage/cost/velocity dashboard remains available.
See the [ownership and qualification contract](architecture/my-work.md).

Protocol94 added [authenticated GitHub search and composer fixes](setup.md#github-requests-and-composer-controls):
private-repository reads use the actual configured account, provider tool IDs
are assigned before ownership is retained, and one Enter sends one ordinary
message even during autosave. Autonomy settings are beside their choices;
profile-wide command families and fenced-code copy controls share
the existing policy and clipboard paths.
It preserves protocol93 [retained PR CI watches](setup.md#retained-pull-request-ci-watches):
exact account/root/head ownership, cross-view deduplication, historical
observations, startup-failure diagnostics and source-bound notifications.
Reopening a pane never restarts polling; uncertain cleanup remains partial.
This source update does not relabel the separately delivered protocol92 DMG.
The [required combination and native-gate map](architecture/milestone-combination-matrix.md)
keeps complete Local/SSH generated coverage separate from missing current
physical SendBox and account-blocked hosted-CI acceptance.

Whole-descendant containment can be required explicitly through **Guardrails /
Require Sandbox** (qualified SendBox) or `moguri containment require-sandbox
--confirm-review`. Ordinary Local/SSH still owns known groups only. Missing
qualification blocks new work; selecting this policy does not silently change
an existing session's Env, qualify an old workload or choose a model.

The macOS app bundles **SendBox 0.2.7 and a compatible pinned Linux worker,
Node runtime and native dependencies**. [Managed setup](architecture/managed-sandbox.md)
replaces developer commands with one explicit in-app review. SendBox 0.2.7 is
the minimum supported release; a saved older selection is blocked until you
explicitly review the bundled setup, never silently upgraded or replaced by
Local. Private workspaces and selected-provider DNS aliases are automatic.
Setup review discloses the broader GitHub Meta network delegation (the SendBox
host caches Meta ranges and seeds each guest; guests never contact Meta).
Public runtime updates stay separate from activation and tool permissions.
The [native combination record](architecture/milestone-combination-matrix.md)
tracks current physical evidence separately from historical runs and the
remaining milestone gates.

Explicitly configured **local OpenAI-compatible models** now share the same
worker, permissions and accounting as Copilot. Endpoint discovery never scans
hosts or downloads weights. [DS4 with DeepSeek V4.1 Flash Q2](architecture/ds4-compatibility.md)
has a real installed-runtime qualification and an explicit, generated-context
compatibility probe. New sessions resolve snapshotted global,
current-profile and project controls, with explicit session overrides and
visible provenance; existing sessions are not rewritten.
[Runtime and hardware inspection](architecture/model-readiness.md) keeps
actual execution-machine observations separate from endpoint availability and
capacity estimates. Exact offline version execution needs a separate one-use
user review; it never starts a model or installs weights.

Automatic **Kupo** exposes Balanced, Savings and Performance as routing modes,
separate from exact shared role-effort and working-window controls. It selects
only compatible actual roles within
the selected boundary; Savings/Performance require reviewed evaluation and
reference-price profiles, never guessed frontier classes. Bounded Cascade and
Critique retain original role results, and text compaction (on by default,
following the shared smart compaction setting) preserves readable history and
source provenance. Finite automatic work uses
complete all-role holds and selected-boundary finishing. The
[owned transport contract](architecture/owned-model-transports.md) keeps
SSH/native bounded decisions and metadata finishing on their original parent;
neither approves code or Local Git. Managed native scheduling can prepare its
source without a model turn. [Snapshot retries and transport checkpoints](architecture/native-retry-checkpoints.md)
add explicit opt-in original-snapshot restaging, separately accepted peer Git
and disclosed native-model/Local-Git publication. Jev/System One still needs a
real bounded output/accounting contract; generated fixtures are not live-model
quality or billing evidence.

[Reviewed candidate resources](architecture/candidate-transports.md) add
pinned-SSH worktrees and native private-snapshot staging, exact project tests
and separately accepted source application. Native implementation remains
behind current released-runtime qualification, not a Local fallback. Private
native acceptance does not publish to Local Git or replace that separate review.

**Settings / Models / Providers** can disable providers or unwanted models per
profile. Matching upstream model IDs share one explicit provider choice, without
duplicates or silent fallback. The same availability gates `/model`, routing and
new calls. Disabling the selected model requires a fresh selection, even after
re-enabling. [Provider/model controls](setup.md#provider-and-model-availability).

Isolated **profiles** use immutable SDK clients over the same local authority.
Desktop's profile selector, TUI **F8** and CLI `--profile ID` preserve separate
accounts, projects, drafts, memory and artifacts. Creating a profile neither
copies data nor selects it. Global environment policy, shared startup
preferences and optional global hard budgets cannot be escaped by switching.
Old owned work stays in its original profile.
Remote writers sharing a pinned peer and canonical workspace serialize across
profile/target aliases and Local mappings; failed-root quarantine survives restart.
Guided questions can include an explicitly labeled current-solver recommendation
without another model call. You still choose the actual answer or tool approval;
advice retains its model provenance and cannot grant permissions.

Context supports project/client text, locally normalized clipboard/file
images, exact reviewed folders, typed GitHub issue/PR references and authorized
session-text snapshots. Unsupported image models preserve the draft/queue
rather than dropping context. Bare attachment prefixes remain literal until
the user selects their source.

The [desktop interaction update](setup.md#desktop-interactions) adds a
compact five-source attachment menu, retained previews/removal, reviewed session
drag-to-attach, persisted session order and confirmation preferences. Use the
whole session row or Alt+Up/Down to reorder siblings, including children.
Dragging a child out asks before detaching, with a saved opt-out in Settings /
Confirmations. Unpin has a crossed-out
pin. Global views live on the left; the right rail contains the session tools
and per-session **Code change** and **Work item** links.
Click an active right-rail icon again to collapse its pane back to the rail.
Terminal belongs to a session: project-free consoles start in configured HOME,
and project consoles keep their bound worktree. There is no global-terminal UI.
Ordinary project-free Local chats also use their
[captured Home](architecture/project-free-execution.md) for approved file
and command tools, without creating a project. Browser control keeps its
explicit user toggle; GitHub commands need an explicit repository target.
Opening Terminal or explicitly switching chats with it visible starts
or reuses the exact selected console; + is independent of unrelated UI work.
Enable local voice in Settings to download the sole pinned model; disabling
voice deletes only that Moguri-managed model. Click the microphone to record
and click again to confirm; hold Ctrl+Space for push-to-talk and release to
finish. Shortcut toggle mode is an explicit setting, independent of the
microphone button and consented focused-composer standby. Words stream into
the draft without an Insert step or automatic
prompt submission. Side chat
opens immediately, read-only, with inherited controls and captured main context.

[Session controls and interactive tools](architecture/session-controls-and-tools.md)
add visible stable IDs, reviewed ID context, success-only dependencies,
same-project bulk actions and pinning, multiple verified PRs with an
Actions/reviews pane, real JS/TS definitions/references, typed array helpers,
isolated interactive HTML and owned Local Playwright/browser screenshots
attached to chat. These are bounded alpha capabilities, not native OS control
or a general-purpose automation engine.

[Chat activity](setup.md#chat-activity-and-usage) uses small operation
icons, expandable original arguments/results, observed timing/output quantities
and live timers. Responses have copy/info actions; the compact budget view puts
estimated USD above tokens/context. Private reasoning and unknown costs are
never invented.

The [Agent terminal tab](setup.md#separate-agent-terminal) shows Moguri's
approved commands and output. The agent can reread its own command history;
the separate User and Global consoles remain private. Commands keep their
existing approvals and per-command PTY lifecycle, not shared shell state.

[Lean tooling](architecture/lean-tooling.md) adds lazy typed discovery,
compact recoverable results, deterministic file/data/document operations and
browser-free search. Root-bound main/child messaging and orchestration preserve
read-only side chats, actual actors, approvals and aggregate budgets. Shared
workflows include `/review`, `/security`, `/performance`, `/debug` and the
[new design, continuation, child-session and critique commands](architecture/command-tool-preferences.md).
Rank equivalent integrations in Settings: Gateway MCP, direct MCP, REST, then
CLI by default. Direct schemas keep the same exact MCP execution approvals.

The [workspace experience](architecture/workspace-experience.md) adds
chart-first **My work, Usage, Cost and Velocity** dashboard pages and a
profile-private **skill gateway** for local folders and refreshed remote
archives. Settings use compact information/copy controls and contain Artifacts,
Candidates and unified Sandbox management. Suggestions offers global local
usage-gap checks; `/suggestions` defaults to the current project's scope.
My work also has the [configured GitHub attention inbox](architecture/my-work.md),
with explicit refresh rather than a recurring scheduler.
Model generation still requires exact source review.
Alerts have a dismissible X without clearing the underlying work or draft.
Read-only Kanban sync retains its exact source across presentation updates;
see the [alert and observation contract](architecture/alerts-kanban-sync.md).
Automations holds recurring automations and one-time scheduled prompts. Work item links the project's Kanban cards or
GitHub issues; session PRs open in Code change. Copilot connection status stays in Settings,
not the left sidebar.

**PDF, Excel (.xlsx) and Word (.docx)** use locally extracted, encrypted
document snapshots with bounded, approved page/section/cell inspection.
Originals stay retained; formulas never execute and scanned PDF pages explicitly
report unavailable OCR. Source/text files, including Java, and images remain
supported. See [document limits and usage](architecture/document-attachments.md).

Implemented model controls offer the model maximum and half maximum, or actual
provider-declared working windows, through the same service contract. Unsupported saved values block
inference without clamping history. Pastes over 50 lines become exact scoped
text files, not whole-paste prompt expansions. Desktop, TUI and the SDK preserve
failed/conflicting unsent pastes; approved bounded file reads work through Local
and pinned SSH workers without modifying a source checkout. See
[usage](setup.md) and the [context boundary](architecture/context-inputs.md).
These context features are implemented. Final native and integrated acceptance
remain separate in the [current roadmap](remaining-milestone-gaps.md).

Core **Remote SSH** execution uses an explicitly pinned host and approved
remote workspace. The existing worker runs inference and file/command tools
there; the local service still owns approvals and history. Disconnect/restart
reconciliation retains late accounting without replaying effects or turning
partial work into success. Files, Git changes and read-only plan views now use
the actual SSH workspace through the same SDK and slash commands.
The local service never substitutes an attached Local checkout for a Remote
workspace or index. Explicit Remote plan saves now bind the
reviewed peer/root/path/digest and run one owned filesystem operation without a
model, preserving independent Remote-boundary snapshots. Stops, lost receipts,
changed scopes and recovery keep partial outcomes honest and never replay writes.
Qualified 0.18.0-alpha.2 adds reviewed peer/resource Remote MCP grants, actual
model/external SSH calls and no-replay retained-result recovery, with shared
CLI/TUI and desktop review/inspection. Forwarding access is separately opt-in;
refresh credentials never leave their backend. This is still an initial
macOS alpha, not the completed first milestone.
Qualified **0.19.0-alpha.1 / protocol 25** also adds explicit Remote user consoles
with captured SSH host/root, original-owner restart recovery and ephemeral
Ghostty/CLI/TUI input. The exact SDK and macOS app are independently qualified;
[setup](setup.md#preserved-qualified-0190-alpha1-checkpoint) records their
immutable identities. No terminal is silently relabeled Local or Sandbox.
Qualified **0.20.0-alpha.1 / protocol 26** also adds reviewed private repository metadata
through the selected SSH host's GitHub CLI account, with retained peer/root/
build provenance, no provider request and no laptop-account fallback.
Its exact installed SDK and actual packaged app are independently qualified;
[setup](setup.md#preserved-qualified-0200-alpha1-checkpoint) records the
immutable identities. At that checkpoint, Remote repository memory remained
unavailable. Qualified **0.21.0-alpha.1 / protocol 27** now adds
session-bound Local/SSH lexical indexing, actual-host freshness checks,
optional model context/direct search and reviewed builtin memory MCP tools.
SDK, CLI, native TUI and desktop share exact peer/root identity and no-replay
index jobs. The exact installed SDK and actual packaged app are independently
qualified; [setup](setup.md#preserved-qualified-0210-alpha1-checkpoint)
records their immutable identities. Old two-tool builtin MCP grants require
fresh review, never silent widening. Earlier archives remain unchanged.
Qualified **0.22.0-alpha.1 / protocol 29** adds a shared Local candidate workflow: explicitly
stage text proposals in a separate clean owned worktree, review again, then
apply only exact base-bound bytes. SDK, CLI, native TUI and desktop preserve
independent history, real user acceptance, raw index/HEAD and partial/restart
outcomes without a model or automatic commit. The exact installed SDK and
actual packaged app are independently qualified;
[setup](setup.md#current-qualified-0220-alpha1-checkpoint) records their
immutable identities. Compound model routing,
finite kupo wind-down and Max still remain unavailable, not implied by the
private Cascade/Critique transport proofs.
Qualified **0.23.0-alpha.1 / protocol 31** adds independently retained planned
budget capacity and one explicitly cost-reviewed, tool-less Local model
proposal through the same SDK/CLI/TUI/desktop. Generated source/provenance and
actual charges remain inspectable; staging and application still need their
two separate reviews. Its exact installed SDK and actual packaged app pass
independent qualification; [setup](setup.md#current-qualified-0230-alpha1-checkpoint)
records immutable identities. This is not completed compound routing or the
first milestone; see [the generation contract](architecture/candidate-generations.md).
The **0.24 source foundation** adds internal complete planned-capacity batch
calculation, not another public model workflow or new native delivery.
Recorded and prospective roles share the same cumulative budget; a failed
whole bound leaves no prefix. The qualified 0.23 archives stay frozen.
Its private acknowledged-role probe reuses the actual worker and budget
transactions, not another model loop. Public compound admission and real-model
quality remain gated.
Qualified **0.25.0-alpha.1 / protocol 32** adds independently retained exact
role observations and shared read-only inspection through source deletion/
restart. Model data is not a user answer, code approval or normal solver
context. Its exact installed SDK and actual packaged app are independently
qualified; [setup](setup.md#current-qualified-0250-alpha1-checkpoint)
records immutable identities. This includes the 0.24 prerequisites, not public
compound scheduling, real-family quality or finite kupo. Earlier archives stay
unchanged.
The **0.26 source** connects those complete retained role envelopes to the
actual control-plane worker, with conservative future contexts and no-replay
ownership. This remains an internal Node primitive, not public compound
scheduling or a new qualified native delivery.
Qualified **0.27.0-alpha.1 / protocol 33** links a final retained proposer to its
canonical candidate origin through shared SDK/CLI/TUI/desktop inspection and
separate staging/application. Its independent copy retains raw model evidence,
not quality or user acceptance. [Setup](setup.md#development-027-canonical-final-role-proposals)
records complete source, independently installed SDK and exact native delivery
qualification and immutable identities. Earlier archives remain frozen.
Qualified **0.28.0-alpha.1 / protocol 34** adds explicit provider-declared Copilot
metadata inspection through the SDK, CLI, native TUI and existing desktop Model
menu. Normal login/discovery/inference is unchanged; unknown family stays
unknown, and declarations never attest independence, quality or approval.
[The contract](architecture/model-evidence.md) and
[setup](setup.md#development-028-explicit-model-declarations) separate its
source, exact installed SDK and actual native qualification from the frozen
0.27 delivery. Earlier archives remain unchanged.
Qualified **0.29.0-alpha.1 / protocol 35** adds explicit output/context contracts to the
existing internal owned executor and shared read-only contract inspection.
Router explanations cannot enter a contracted solver's selected context;
rejected or malformed advice stays charged and cannot start the next role.
This is not public compound scheduling, independent-family proof or acceptance.
[The contract](architecture/owned-role-contracts.md) records complete
source, independently installed SDK and actual native qualification. The
qualified 0.28 artifacts remain frozen.

**Milestone 1 is accepted** at protocol 106 with SendBox 0.2.7: all 10,080
required Local/SSH/Sandbox cells, ten physical native gates and the full
source, hidden desktop, SDK and package runs pass. Regression runs now use a
78-cell covering array; the full product is opt-in `npm run test:matrix`
([D38](architecture/decisions.md#d38-covering-array-milestone-regression)). The
[acceptance record and roadmap](remaining-milestone-gaps.md) maps every
milestone criterion to its evidence, records the user-directed replacement of
account-blocked hosted CI with local evidence, and lists the remaining roadmap
owned by [#39](https://github.com/mbianchidev/moguri/issues/39). It is still a
development alpha: not signed, notarized or publicly distributed.

The earlier issue-17 checkpoint used **protocol 37** for shared model windows, scoped
long-paste files and reviewed SendBox execution. SDK, CLI/TUI and hidden
desktop run the same qualified private-stage worker, Manual decisions, budget
ledger, exact-owner stop/recovery and separate actual-user source publication.
Actual guest/control-loss checks retain partial work and unknown usage without
replay. [Setup](setup.md#native-servicesdk-development-checkpoint) records
the generated provider evidence and remaining gates; this is not a replacement
for frozen archives, live-model quality or full first-milestone acceptance.

Chats can have **no project**, without inheriting any workspace root or coding
tools. One desktop **Start** chooser offers a new chat, an existing project,
local-folder import or explicit repository clone. General conversations live
under **Chats**. `/suggestions` previews scoped prior prompts before model analysis;
**ask Moguri** and `/meta` open a settings chat whose changes require exact human review.
MCP HTTP servers support explicit **OAuth with PKCE**, resource-bound keychain
credentials and refresh. Shared question, approval and done indicators appear
in both clients. Desktop OS banners are off by default and use generic content
unless the user opts into previews.

The desktop composer is an icon toolbar: attach, environment, model name,
autonomy, unlimited-budget/usage, microphone and paper-plane Send. Holding
Cmd/Ctrl turns idle Send into a queue clock; active turns show a red Stop icon
in that same slot. A blocked session uses a Resume/play control there instead,
preserving the unsent draft; inspect effects before continuing. Enter uses the
current action; Shift+Enter adds a line.
Both sidebars resize, and message copy appears on hover or keyboard focus.
Toggle/dropdown preferences, model context and supported thinking effort save
automatically through shared SDK controls; text settings retain explicit saves.
Model switches preserve the original effort preference, with a supported
fallback and restoration on capable models, not a reset to Model default.
`/thinking` and `/effort` set supported effort; `/context-window` sets an exact
token ceiling or `min`, `half`, `max` without running a model.
See [desktop controls and settings](setup.md#shared-sdk-and-settings).

New chats can use a fixed **global default model/effort** or the current
profile's **last explicit selection**. Existing chats and higher-priority
overrides stay unchanged. See [model defaults](architecture/model-controls.md#new-session-model-defaults).

The session workspace adds **queue-only Cmd/Ctrl+Enter**, shared chat slash
commands, enforced read-only sessions and parallel question-only side chats.
Opening Side chat immediately gives the same composer, model/thinking controls
and voice input with captured main-chat context, permanently read-only.
Hold **Ctrl+Space** to dictate locally: words stream into the textbox and release
flushes them without sending. The microphone button instead uses click-to-record,
click-again-to-confirm, never press-and-hold. Session names and settings support fuzzy search.
Desktop embeds **Ghostty** through `ghostty-web`, alongside local diffs, plans,
isolated browser previews, linked PRs and Insights. Double-click a session to
rename it. Sessions support pin/group/
attach/unread/archive/delete actions; project settings and optional archived
retention share the same SDK. Permanent session deletion also deletes its
originating candidates and generation proposals; archiving alone preserves them.
Fresh verification of an exact linked PR's merge also cleans up its candidates.
Ordinary artifacts, applied code, worktrees and external PRs survive. See
[candidate retention](architecture/candidate-cleanup.md). A terminal is an explicit Local or pinned SSH
user console, not an agent permission or a claimed sandbox.

The Local **Browser** pane also supports approved agent navigation, inspection,
clicks and text input. Its top **Agent control** switch starts off and revokes
access immediately when disabled. It never adopts a personal browser.
See [browser control](architecture/agent-browser.md).

Attachments stay compact in the composer/chat. Clicking an image opens the
large, uncropped viewer without changing captured context.

Project-free sessions can open private HOME consoles without granting model
workspace access. Project-free Autopilot cannot invent workspace access, and side
chats expose an explicit concrete-model selector when needed.
User consoles retain authenticated per-profile/peer owners across
explicit service restart or controller loss. Ghostty and shared SDK/CLI/TUI
inspection reattach the same process, never replay input or automatically
replace an old console. Ordinary service stop closes known groups; private
cleanup failures retain explicit retryable intent. Output stays bounded and
volatile, not conversation/model context. See the
[Local ownership](architecture/terminal-reattachment.md) and
[Remote ownership](architecture/remote-user-consoles.md) boundaries.

**Managed Local worktrees** isolate branch checkouts without moving the attached
base folder or index. Create, discover, inspect, open and safely remove them
through the shared SDK, CLI/TUI or project settings. Worker tools, Files,
Changes, Plan, terminals, memory and dependency installs resolve the same bound
root. Writers serialize within a root; different worktrees can run concurrently.
Removal requires a clean, idle, unbound owned checkout and preserves its branch.
Discovery does not adopt or grant access to unmanaged worktrees.

**Independent artifacts** retain plans, decisions, answers, research notes and
reports with revisions and actual source provenance. Create them without a
conversation, or explicitly retain a completed user/model/tool result. Each has
its own encrypted retention grant. Project removal previews the exact set and
requires retain, export-then-delete or delete; ordinary documents survive session
retention. Candidate/proposal reports are the explicit session-owned exception.
Real structured clarifications record actual user answers and retain them by
default, with an explicit opt-out. Answers never grant tool/Git permissions.
Desktop [answer controls](architecture/session-interactions.md#direct-question-answers)
use a scrollable choice list and a blank Other field that sends on Enter.
Documents can associate with profile folders and project work items. Explicit
reviewed repository copies preserve complete history under `artifacts/`, with an
optional new local Git branch. No checkout, push or unrelated staging changes;
project deletion re-verifies the actual copy and any requested commit.

Dictation uses local NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 through a pinned native runtime. The
user explicitly accepts and downloads the model once. NVIDIA documents
**40 locales: 19 ready, 13 broad coverage, 8 adaptation-only**, not 22 verified
ready languages. No cloud ASR fallback or automatic model-weight download occurs.
You can instead trust an existing streaming model file, such as a Nemotron
streaming GGUF or Handy's Parakeet/Moonshine streaming GGUF; Moguri locks its
SHA-256, asks again if it changes and never deletes it
([setup](setup.md#use-an-existing-streaming-model-file)).

Projects also have a **local Kanban** for feature, bug and misc tickets, with
their own board chat, shared Show/Hide preference and same-panel GitHub/Linear
sources, per-column creation and drag/drop. `/continue-work` or the prompt
**continue work** asks each time whether to use Kanban or send the prompt
normally. Kanban takes one eligible item in an isolated Local checkout
through its draft PR; it does not merge or drain the backlog. Project secondary
click opens actions; dragging or Alt+Up/Down reorders. Work item can select a
Kanban card. [Setup and boundaries](architecture/project-kanban.md).
**Sync with GitHub** updates linked status into Kanban only and can optionally
import open repository issues. Draft PRs mean in progress, ready PRs mean review,
and completed/won't-do closed issues mean done. Optional Linear imports start off, use a
user-supplied keychain credential and never upload local tickets.

The **shared dependency cache** reuses SHA-512-verified archives across projects
and branches, with npm and pnpm adapters. Exact lock/manifest plans and fresh
OSV advisory checks gate downloads and reuse. Managed installs block lifecycle
scripts and hooks, use private staging and keep mutable trees worktree-local.
This is not a malware-free guarantee; script execution stays unavailable until
a real SendBox boundary is qualified.

This is a **macOS development alpha** that completes Milestone 1; it is not a signed, notarized public release.
Explicit **estimate-based token/USD caps** and separate profile/global hard
policies now share cumulative role-aware reservations. Unknown completion holds
capacity; deletion, defaults and restart do not refund it. Named Copilot/reseller
models can use **originating-provider API-equivalent estimates**, not subscription
bills. Finite USD needs a fresh user rate or explicit reference-rate consent;
missing/stale prices remain unknown. These are admission
limits, not exact provider-billing guarantees. CLI/TUI, desktop composer,
settings and the profile usage dashboard share the SDK.
Dashboard views now add UTC presets/year/custom ranges, calendar buckets,
captured price history and retained per-call/owning-turn records. Observed
stream delivery metrics disclose missing coverage and are not GPU-throughput
or productivity claims; cache subsets never inflate reported totals.
Tool/MCP outcomes now have a sanitized, session-independent ledger with an
explicit known-result failure rate and separate denied/stopped/partial/unknown
counts. Dashboard, CLI/TUI and SDK also expose current-profile key-backed
ciphertext sizes, not physical disk usage or reclaimed space. Earlier deleted
tool history remains unavailable.
Repository/organization/visibility filters now use explicitly refreshed,
root-bound GitHub metadata and immutable per-admission snapshots. Every tagged
step rechecks its actual Local/SSH Git origin. Unknown history is not backfilled,
and the open-source category is explicitly public plus detected OSI-approved
license metadata, not a legal review or a synonym for public.

**Reviewed text-context compaction** now uses one explicitly authorized,
tool-less Local/SSH model call through the same SDK. Previewing does not infer;
generation, actual history/content review, apply/discard and original-context
restore are separate actions. Complete recent turns, original encrypted history
and drafts remain retained; rejected/unknown calls still count. Desktop exposes
review under Model, and CLI/TUI share `/compact`. Images and implicit kupo
compactor selection are not supported.

**Smart compaction** is on by default: when a chat nears its model's working
window (75%, or 200k tokens), Moguri summarizes older turns with that chat's
model in one metered call and keeps going, with original history restorable.
Type `/compact` to compact now. Built-in slash commands always win over a skill
with the same name, and Moguri asks you to rename such skills.

[**Kupo**](architecture/automatic-kupo.md) is always in the model picker.
Its automatic policy uses configured models: none blocks inference, one runs
directly in Single, and multiple models support task-based Single, gated
Cascade or eligible read-only Critique with one revision. Declared capability
categories guide routing, including pools of three through twenty models.
Only the selected response reaches normal approvals; every actual role is
metered. Independent critique still needs reviewed lineage evidence. Finite
automatic budgets, images, synthetic tuning and Sandbox routing remain
unavailable without fallback. Existing explicit
[Single policies](architecture/routing.md) remain supported separately.

[Reviewed **Local Cascade/Critique**](architecture/compound-workflows.md)
now has a shared development service/SDK, CLI, actual TUI and desktop path.
An actual classifier binds a declared concrete route; tool-less proposals retain
the task plan, architecture and implementation. Actual-user review separately
authorizes staging and exact project tests in distinct owned worktrees.
Failed drafts remain isolated, and a recommended candidate still needs its
separate source-application review. Reviewed lineage sources are limited user
policy claims, not proof of independent training or calibrated quality.

Finite Local routing now reserves one actual metadata-only finishing role and
has separately reviewed actual-user accepted-work checkpoint branches that
preserve the source index/HEAD. A summary never accepts code or approves Git.
[Local **Autopilot Max**](architecture/owned-decisions.md) now uses an
explicitly configured bounded-model System One-compatible alternative with
fixed or Single-routed solvers. Exact existing tool delegation, user-declared
technical choices and bounded safe-boundary steering share the real model
ledger and cancellation owner. The actual actor remains `decision-provider`,
not the user; human intervention and hard policy win. Jev itself remains
blocked where its documented API cannot enforce the required output bound.
No generative substitution or calibrated reliability is claimed.

The current generated source, packed SDK and exact native image pass the
[full acceptance sweep](setup.md#final-protocol-40-source-acceptance).
Live-provider/calibrated-quality gates, complete remote/native
side-panel/extension transport, Remote/native compound/Max and
remote/native wind-down remain incomplete.
Unknown usage and Copilot billing are not presented as zero cost.
Manual remains the default. Guided still needs human confirmation; Autopilot
can use only explicit bounded user grants. SendBox has a visible fail-closed
configuration/readiness surface. The development SDK/client lifecycle
now passes actual native generated-provider checks, but readiness still needs
explicit reviewed release/image/network pins and private staging. Endpoint-only
cold networking remains blocked; no alias or Local fallback is added
automatically. Installing SendBox alone does not enable native execution.

```bash
npm ci
npm run build
npm start -- --project /absolute/path/to/project
```

Run `npm run desktop` in another terminal to open the same sessions in desktop.
In the TUI, **Ctrl+L** starts Copilot sign-in, **Ctrl+M** selects a model, and
**Ctrl+K** shows commands. Desktop exposes the same setup in **GitHub Copilot**.
Complete GitHub's device authorization yourself; Moguri does not read IDE login
files or require another provider's API key.

See [setup and usage](setup.md), the [SDK API and CLI](sdk.md),
the [initial architecture](architecture/overview.md),
and [Phase 0 evidence and remaining release blockers](architecture/phase-zero.md).
The [session workspace contract](architecture/session-workspace.md) records
Ghostty qualification, deletion/recovery and project-policy boundaries.
The [engagement contract](architecture/engagement.md) records OAuth,
project-free isolation, suggestions, reviewed configuration and notifications.
The [runtime foundation](architecture/runtime-foundation.md) records local
models/defaults and the genuine SendBox qualification blocker; [typed inputs](architecture/context-inputs.md)
records snapshot consent and image/source boundaries.
The [managed workspace contract](architecture/managed-workspaces.md)
records Local ownership, root consistency and partial-operation reconciliation.
`npm run package:mac` produces an ad-hoc-signed development app, DMG and ZIP under
`release/`. It is not a notarized distribution.
The app includes the CLI, TUI and their shared Node runtime. Copying it does not
start the TUI or add a shell command. Use **Settings > General > Command line >
Install `moguri` command**, then follow the [PATH setup instructions](setup.md#macos-command-line-installation).
That guide also documents removal, moved-app recovery and the manual workaround
for older builds.
CI runs only on pushes to `main`, not pull requests or feature branches.
The explicit 30-minute cap is removed; GitHub-hosted jobs still have the
[platform's six-hour limit](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/limits).

The in-app updater follows the upstream `mbianchidev/moguri` GitHub Releases.
Public releases are checked, verified and staged without a token, so once the
repository is public, packaged apps update automatically, and installs still
wait for your confirmation. An optional read-only token covers the private
period and GitHub's rate limit; see [GitHub updates](settings/general.md#github-updates).

Settings has a shorter rail: 7 groups and 28 entries, down from 11 groups and
37. Integrations and Interface are each one rail entry with keyboard-navigable
tabs, and each integration tab shows its status. See
[Settings rail structure](design.md#settings-rail-structure).
